newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH stock rallies after meeting.
newsitem.headline: LVMH stock rallies after meeting.

text.p: Shares in LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton rose to a fresh year high on Thursday after the chairmen of British drinks groups Guinness and Grand Met agreed to consider LVMH chairman's Bernard Arnault's proposal to blend the three companies' drinks businesses.

"By putting pressure on the legal front and through the stockmarket, Bernard Arnault has managed to turn the situation around. He's obliged the British companies to look at his plan. The market is applauding his success," a broker said.
The stock was up 4.87 percent at 1,657 francs at 1320 GMT, outperforming the CAC-40 index which was up 1.1 percent.
"Arnault has scored a point but it's premature to talk of victory," another broker said.

Share analysts say Arnault must now prove that his proposal to set up a stand-alone, listed drinks business will create more value for the shareholders of all three companies than the planned 24 billion pound Guinness-Grand Met merger.
Arnault has a good track record in terms of creating shareholder value -- between 1992 and 1996, LVMH shares have been the biggest gainers of the CAC-40 components.
In the past 12 months, the stock has risen 30 percent but lagged other blue chips such as Elf Aquitaine, up 67.5 percent, L'Oreal, up 59 percent, Carrefour, up 58 percent, and Total, up 56 percent.
Brokers said foreigners were big buyers on Thursday of LVMH, which has see-sawed since the company began buying Grand Met stock in mid-June to force the British companies to negotiate.
In the past two weeks, LVMH has spent more than eight billion francs to buy 6.4 percent of Grand Met in an apparent bid to line up votes to block the merger.

LVMH previously took legal action against Guinness -- in which it holds 14.2 percent -- to defend its right to buy Guinness out of their valuable distribution ventures, which hold the rights to market Guinness brands in France, the United States and much of the Far East for 10 years.
Brokers said another factor contributing to the demand for LVMH is the dollar's strength against the franc.
